findings.description: The bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration block, so objects (including the vendor roster spreadsheet uploaded via aws_s3_bucket_object.reports_seed_object) are stored unencrypted by default, violating encryption-at-rest requirements for potentially sensitive reporting data.
This bucket stores ledger/financial export data but defines no server_side_encryption_configuration, leaving highly sensitive financial data unencrypted at rest.
The bucket enables versioning and logging but has no server_side_encryption_configuration, so model artifacts are stored without encryption at rest.
The bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration block, leaving operational runbook content (which may include sensitive operational details or credentials references) unencrypted at rest.
The object is uploaded to a bucket lacking default encryption and does not specify its own server_side_encryption/kms_key_id, so this seed data file is persisted in cleartext.
